WHERE THE GAPS APPEAR

Hub service coverage

Share of essential energy demand supplied in each scenario.

What “stress-aware” means

For each possible battery count at each hub, the model simulates all three cases. It takes that hub's lowest fraction of equivalent service-hours and multiplies it by planned duration, assumed occupancy, and the user-set priority. Dynamic programming finds the allocation with the highest sum of these conservative scores.

This is a sum of per-hub worst cases. It is not a probabilistic forecast or a proof of the best plan for every possible outage. A longer outage is capped at 60 hours. A service floor, when enabled, must hold across all three cases in stress-aware mode.

Transparent inputs, explicit trade-offs, and results you can reproduce.

01

A community allocation decision

GridRelief helps a community coordinator explore where a limited inventory of portable batteries might sustain essential services during an outage. It recommends pack counts, simulates hourly supply, and compares that plan with a round-robin baseline.

The six default hubs, their names, occupancy assumptions, electrical loads, solar installations, and priority weights are illustrative. They do not represent verified Charlotte facilities, shelter capacity, neighborhood demographics, or an emergency service.

People stay in control

Weights represent planning choices, not a ranking of people's value. The service floor lets users demand a minimum at every hub. Results require review by the affected community and qualified electrical professionals before real use.

02

Hourly energy conservation

Solar serves loads first. Surplus charges storage; a deficit discharges storage subject to its energy, reserve, efficiency, and power limits. Unmet demand is recorded, never hidden.

PV kW = array kWp × GHI / 1000 × 0.80
usable discharge = (stored − reserve) × √η
initial + solar = served + spill + losses + ending

GHI is horizontal irradiance, not a detailed tilted-panel PV forecast. The 0.80 performance factor is an editable-code simplification. Charge and discharge each use the square root of round-trip efficiency. Separate compatible PV and battery inverters are assumed.

Cooling scales with temperature; lighting uses day/night factors. These are transparent training assumptions, not calibrated building models. “Equivalent service-hours” is the sum of hourly served/demand fractions. Occupancy-weighted scores are not counts of people reached or lives protected.

03

Exact optimization, bounded claims

Precomputed hourly simulations give a score for every possible pack count at each hub. An integer dynamic program allocates all available packs to maximize the chosen score while enforcing the selected service floor.

The state is (hub index, packs used). The search costs O(hubs × packs²), after the simulations. It is exact for this discrete model and separable objective; it does not certify field performance. The round-robin baseline first satisfies the same minimum packs at each hub, then cycles remaining packs in listed order.

What the model leaves out

Installation time, travel, wiring compatibility, inrush currents, thermal comfort, medical requirements, battery degradation, weather probability, feeder topology, equipment failures, and emergency operations. Essential loads are served proportionally as a bundle. Do not use this prototype to operate life-support equipment or decide evacuation.

04

Data, sources & privacy

Default weather is a frozen synthetic daylight and temperature curve. The optional weather button retrieves four days of hourly temperature and shortwave radiation for the fixed Charlotte coordinates (35.2271, −80.8431), beginning at midnight on forecast day one in America/New_York.

Weather is model output from Open-Meteo, not an observation or outage warning. The configured solar factor and stress multipliers still apply. Imported forecast snapshots retain their retrieval time; old snapshots are labeled as saved data.

  • NREL/DOE · Resilient operations of solar-plus-storage community hubs (2024) ↗
  • REopt · Established site-level energy optimization reference ↗
  • Open-Meteo · Forecast API, variable definitions & attribution ↗
  • Open-Meteo · Noncommercial free endpoint terms ↗

Scenarios are stored in this browser only. No account, analytics, secrets, geolocation request, or device control. Weather calls disclose only this fixed city's coordinates plus normal request metadata to the provider. Exported files contain your scenario, including any hub names you enter.
